methodology: National accounts PFCE by purpose (COICOP) where available; household survey data otherwise. % of total private household consumption expenditure. NOT GDP; NOT per-capita GDP. Sources listed per market.

markets.source: MOSPI National Accounts Statistics, Table 21.2 (2022-23 series, COICOP 2018), current prices. URL: mospi.gov.in. Computed shares via lisp_eval from Rs Crore figures.
markets.note: Transport unusually high (17.4%) because India's COICOP includes purchase of vehicles under transport. Health 5.4% is private out-of-pocket; public health excluded. India food share in national accounts (28.3%) is LOWER than in household surveys (43% rural, 39% urban HCES 2022-23) because national accounts use a different deflator and include imputed housing rent. Use with caution.

markets.source: Philippine Statistics Authority, Family Income and Expenditure Survey (FIES) 2023, via CEIC Data. psa.gov.ph.
markets.note: FIES 2023 food = 41.8% (derived from avg food expenditure / avg total expenditure from CEIC). Transport 6.78%, education 3.3%. Health and recreation not separately reported in the CEIC series reviewed. GAP for health, recreation, communication.

markets.source: Statistics South Africa Income and Expenditure Survey 2022-2023, UNICEF-StatsSA analysis (ZAF-UNICEF-trends-cost-living-2025.pdf), Table showing COICOP shares by decile; all-household average derived.
markets.note: All-household average read from the UNICEF/StatsSA table (last column). Health not directly identified in the CEIC column labels; included in 'Other' or 'Miscellaneous G&S'. GAP for health separately. Transport 16.3% includes vehicle purchase. South Africa's USDA food share (21.4% in 2017) is consistent with survey data.

markets.source: BPS Susenas (National Socioeconomic Survey) — annual, but COICOP breakdown at national level is in the BPS Statistical Yearbook; direct extract not available from public search. USDA ERS food share 33.5% (2023 national accounts). This row uses USDA food + ICP 2021 PPP-based category proxies.
markets.note: GAP: health, education, transport, communication, recreation all NOT AVAILABLE from public sources at the category level. BPS publishes Susenas with food/non-food split but the full COICOP breakdown requires the paid Statistical Yearbook or direct BPS access.

markets.source: General Statistics Office, Vietnam Household Living Standards Survey (VHLSS). Published periodically. USDA food share 34.9% (2023).
markets.note: GAP: VHLSS category breakdown exists (WHO/WB cited health ~6-7% in Vietnam circa 2018) but no 2022-23 official COICOP table was located in public search results. Vietnam health spending: WHO Global Health Expenditure Database shows out-of-pocket at ~37% of current health expenditure, roughly 3-4% of household income.

markets.source: CAPMAS Household Income and Expenditure and Consumption Survey (HIECS). USDA food share 36.9% (2023). Note: Egypt experienced 40%+ food inflation 2022-2023 following EGP devaluation.
markets.note: GAP: full COICOP breakdown from CAPMAS HIECS not publicly available. Egypt's rising food share 2017-2023 (+3.3pp) reflects food-price inflation more than income effects — per the 'against-grain mover' finding in chapter 3.

markets.source: USDA ERS (via Our World in Data). National-accounts proxy for food share. GDP PPP: World Bank NY.GDP.PCAP.PP.KD 2023.
markets.note: ANOMALY vs model: Nigeria GDP $7,843 PPP puts it inside the estimated break CI ($5,545–$7,650), which predicts food share ~37%. Actual: 59%, flat since 2017. The 22pp gap reflects two distinct economies: Lagos/Abuja elites (low food share) and 80%+ population in near-subsistence conditions (high food share). Additionally, chronic food-price inflation (30%+ in 2023 post-naira devaluation) forces budget compression even as nominal income stagnates. Nigeria is an against-the-grain mover; the Engel mechanism is overwhelmed by inequality and inflation. COICOP category breakdown: NOT AVAILABLE (NBS Nigeria Food Survey 2022 was released but full COICOP breakdown not in public search results).

markets.source: Statistics South Africa Income and Expenditure Survey (IES) 2022-23, via UNICEF-StatsSA analysis (ZAF-UNICEF-trends-cost-living-2025.pdf). Already in Phase 2 transition-market section; included here for Africa completeness.
markets.note: South Africa is POST-transition (GDP $13,251 PPP, food 21.3%). Its Africa peers are still far behind it. JSE is the most developed stock exchange in sub-Saharan Africa. Health not separately identified in the StatsSA columns reviewed (possibly embedded in 'Miscellaneous G&S'). Full IES 2022-23 microdata available via DataFirst (CC-BY).

markets.source: USDA ERS (via Our World in Data). GDP PPP: World Bank 2023.
markets.note: Kenya 2023 food share 42.1% is a remarkable drop from 56.6% (2022) and 58.7% (2020). If this reflects genuine income-driven consumption shift, Kenya may be entering the transition now. However, a 14.5pp single-year drop is large and may partly reflect post-pandemic recomposition or methodology change. The USDA series for Kenya should be verified against KNBS (Kenya National Bureau of Statistics) household surveys before strong conclusions. At GDP $5,692 PPP, Kenya is just below the bootstrap 90% CI lower bound for the break ($5,545). COICOP breakdown: GAP — full COICOP not publicly available from KNBS in this search.

markets.source: INEGI ENIGH 2022 (microdata via FAO/INEGI). Health share: peer-reviewed paper PMC12924604 citing ENIGH 2000-2022 series (HE as share of total expenditure ~4.9%). Food: USDA ERS 2023 (25.7%).
markets.note: Mexico is solidly post-transition (GDP $21,912 PPP, food 25.7% USDA, 32.1% fitted model). Health share 4.9% of total household expenditure (ENIGH 2022 via academic paper, for households with any health spending). Full COICOP breakdown from ENIGH 2022 microdata is public via INEGI but was not extracted in this search — transport, education, communication are GAP. Mexico's ENIGH follows COICOP categories; microdata available at inegi.org.mx. ENIGH 2024 was conducted (Aug-Nov 2024); results likely available in 2025.

markets.source: IBGE Pesquisa de Orçamentos Familiares (POF) 2017-2018, 58,000 households. Published via IBGE News Agency. Food+housing+transport = 72.2% of total. USDA food share 2023: 16.2%. World Bank report (doi:10.1596/1813-9450-9598) citing POF 2017-18.
markets.note: Brazil is post-transition (GDP $20,025 PPP, food 15.7% urban/23.8% rural, national avg ~17-18%). Transport 18% (includes vehicles); education 4.7% urban vs 2.3% rural — large urban/rural gap. Health not separately reported in the IBGE press release reviewed. Note: food share in POF 2017-18 is significantly lower than USDA 2023 (16.2%) because POF urban average differs from national accounts. Brazil's new POF 2022-2023 is currently in field; results not yet published as of late 2026. Housing (moradia) is the largest expenditure category in Brazil alongside food+transport.

markets.source: USDA ERS (via Our World in Data) for food share. INDEC ENGHo (Encuesta Nacional de Gastos de los Hogares) 2017-18 was the last full survey; no new ENGHo published due to statistical capacity issues. USDA food 2023: 23.1%.
markets.note: Argentina is deeply post-transition on the GDP-PPP metric ($27,847), but chronic inflation (100%+ in 2022-2023, then stabilisation under Milei) distorts all budget-share data. The 23.1% food share reflects nominal spending patterns under hyperinflationary conditions where food prices rose fastest. INDEC suspended the ENGHo after 2017-18; there is no comparable full COICOP survey for 2022-2023. Argentina is analytically post-transition but practically unstable — the Engel mechanism is overwhelmed by macro volatility. FULL COICOP BREAKDOWN: GAP.
